items.q: A 68-year-old man vomits a litre of fresh blood with melaena and shock despite two units. Endoscopy cannot see past clots in the duodenal bulb. CT angiography shows an active gastroduodenal blush. Which catheter target best suits this shocked duodenal re-bleeder after failed endoscopy?
o: Gastroduodenal sandwich coils front and back
Aortic stent-graft for a duodenal ulcer
items.exp:
**Answer: A - Gastroduodenal sandwich coils front and back.** Arcades refill single-sided blocks from behind, so both ends of the bleeding trunk shut together.
**Why the others are wrong**
- B: Aortic grafts miss duodenal branches
- C: Shock cannot wait for re-bleeds
- D: Coronaries ignore gut bleeding
**Key point:** Duodenal re-bleeds need gastroduodenal sandwich.
items.kp: Failed-endoscopy duodenal bleeds need gastroduodenal sandwich coils.

items.q: A 55-year-old woman oozes diffusely from the gastric fundus at third endoscopy with no single vessel to clip. She stays unstable with ongoing transfusion. Which empiric territory best suits this diffuse fundal oozing without a focal blush?
o: Left gastric embolisation for diffuse fundal beds
items.exp:
**Answer: A - Left gastric embolisation for diffuse fundal beds.** The left gastric feeds the fundus diffusely where empiric closure calms oozing no clip can grasp.
**Why the others are wrong**
- B: Femoral ligation starves legs vainly
- C: Brains ignore gastric oozing
- D: Iron never stops active bleeding
**Key point:** Diffuse fundal oozing takes left gastric closure.
items.kp: Diffuse fundal oozing suits empiric left gastric embolisation.

items.q: A 62-year-old man has a jejunal diverticular blush from a vasa recta branch on selective angiography. The operator advances a microcatheter beyond the arcade before coiling. Which tip-position rule best protects bowel when coiling vasa recta branches?
o: Advance beyond arcades since vasa recta are end arteries
Coil the main mesenteric trunk always
Block the aorta for jejunal blushes
items.exp:
**Answer: A - Advance beyond arcades since vasa recta are end arteries.** Proximal blocks infarct long segments while distal tips sacrifice only the bleeding twig.
**Why the others are wrong**
- B: Trunk coils infarct whole territories
- C: Aortas never treat jejunal twigs
- D: Microcatheters protect bowel best
**Key point:** Vasa recta work stays superselective.
items.kp: Mesenteric bleeding needs superselective tips beyond arcades.

items.q: A 70-year-old woman develops severe abdominal pain with rising lactate and peritonism twelve hours after mesenteric embolisation. Her abdomen guards rigidly with absent bowel sounds. Which feared aftermath does pain with lactate and peritonism after bowel embolisation signal?
o: Bowel infarction needing urgent surgical review
Contrast allergy half a day later
items.exp:
**Answer: A - Bowel infarction needing urgent surgical review.** Dead bowel leaks and poisons quickly, so peritonism with lactate after mesenteric work means surgeons at once.
**Why the others are wrong**
- B: Cramps never rigidify abdomens
- C: Allergy strikes within minutes
- D: Success never causes peritonism
**Key point:** Peritonism with lactate means infarcted bowel.
items.kp: Pain with lactate after bowel embolisation means infarction.

items.q: A 58-year-old man re-bleeds massively three days after apparently successful gut embolisation. He is resuscitated again while the team plans next steps. Which re-bleed protocol comes first in this post-embolisation re-bleeder?
o: Repeat angiography re-mapping for new feeders
Stopping all transfusion to test resolve
Declaring the case untreatable at once
items.exp:
**Answer: A - Repeat angiography re-mapping for new feeders.** Fresh collaterals replace sealed ones, so re-mapping finds the new culprit before surgeons open.
**Why the others are wrong**
- B: Blind surgery misses mapped targets
- C: Stopping blood kills re-bleeders
- D: Most re-bleeds yield to re-mapping
**Key point:** Re-bleeds re-map first.
items.kp: Post-embolisation re-bleeds need repeat angiography first.

items.q: A 64-year-old woman has ongoing melaena with a negative catheter angiogram after positive CT. She remains unstable despite resuscitation. Which empiric logic best justifies treating the likely bed despite the negative selective study?
o: Intermittent bleeders hide between injections while beds stay guilty
Negative studies prove bleeding stopped forever
items.exp:
**Answer: A - Intermittent bleeders hide between injections while beds stay guilty.** Arteries spasm and clot between shots, so the CT-proven territory still merits empiric closure.
**Why the others are wrong**
- B: Negatives miss intermittent flow
- C: CT blushes convict territories
- D: Instability demands treatment
**Key point:** Negative angiograms still allow empiric beds.
items.kp: CT-positive unstable bleeders merit empiric embolisation.

items.q: A 52-year-old man has a bleeding rectal Dieulafoy lesion with limited endoscopic access. The superior rectal branch shows the blush. The operator picks coils over particles. Which rectal-agent logic best explains coils over particles in rectal beds?
o: Coils spare collateral rectal networks that particles would shower
items.exp:

- C: Magic never guides agents
- D: Showers necrose rectal walls
**Key point:** Rectal bleeds favour coils over particles.
items.kp: Rectal bleeding favours coils over particles.

items.q: A 75-year-old man on anticoagulation bleeds from a colonic diverticulum with a visible vasa recta blush. Surgery carries prohibitive risk. Which risk-balanced logic best supports superselective coiling in this anticoagulated diverticular bleeder?
o: Tiny distal coils stop bleeds where surgery would kill
items.exp:

- C: Diverticula bleed massively often

items.kp: Anticoagulated diverticular bleeds suit superselective coils.

items.q: A 60-year-old woman develops a tight colonic stricture six months after mesenteric embolisation, with healed ischaemia on biopsy. She obstructs intermittently. Which late aftermath best explains stricture months after bowel embolisation?
o: Healed ischaemia scarring into late stricture
items.exp:
**Answer: A - Healed ischaemia scarring into late stricture.** Sub-lethal ischaemia heals by fibrosis that contracts over months, narrowing the bowel late.
**Why the others are wrong**
- B: Coils never seed cancers
- C: Success still scars mildly
- D: Biopsies sample rather than stricture
**Key point:** Late strictures mark healed ischaemia.
items.kp: Late strictures follow healed bowel ischaemia.

items.q: A 66-year-old man has end-stage liver disease with a bleeding duodenal ulcer and failed endoscopy. His clotting is poor with platelets 40. The team corrects factors before angiography. Which correction logic best precedes gut embolisation in coagulopathic liver disease?
o: Correct clotting enough for safe puncture without delaying rescue
Ignore clotting since radiology is bloodless
Cancel bleeding control for abnormal labs
items.exp:
**Answer: A - Correct clotting enough for safe puncture without delaying rescue.** Access needs workable clotting while bleeding cannot wait for perfect numbers, balancing both urgencies.
**Why the others are wrong**
- B: Endless transfusion delays rescue
- C: Punctures bleed without clotting
- D: Labs never veto rescue
**Key point:** Coagulopathic bleeders correct-then-proceed.
items.kp: Coagulopathic gut bleeders correct clotting then proceed.

items.q: A 49-year-old man bleeds from a jejunal gastrointestinal stromal tumour with a rich single feeding trunk. Surgery is planned next week after bleeding control. Which bridge logic best supports preoperative embolisation for this bleeding stromal tumour?

No bridge needed with blind waiting

- C: Blind waiting bleeds further

items.kp: Bleeding tumours bridge to planned resection.

items.q: A 71-year-old woman has a bleeding duodenal diverticulum beside the papilla with the bile duct nearby. The operator uses tiny coils with extreme care. Which neighbour-protection logic best guides peri-papillary duodenal work near the bile duct?

items.q: A 56-year-old man has obscure mid-gut bleeding with negative endoscopies from both ends. Capsule study points to the ileum. The team plans provocative-free mesenteric mapping. Which obscure-bleed logic best sequences capsule before catheters in mid-gut bleeding?

items.q: A 63-year-old woman has a bleeding colonic angiodysplasia cluster in the caecum with a single feeding arcade. The operator weighs resection against embolisation. Which frailty logic best favours embolisation for caecal angiodysplasia in unfit patients?

items.q: A 59-year-old man has a post-polypectomy bleed with a visible stalk vessel spurting on sigmoidoscopy. Clips fail to grasp the retracted stump. Which rescue logic best positions radiology after failed endoscopic clips for stalk bleeding?

More clips on air without vision
Colonic resection for every polyp bleed

items.q: A 67-year-old woman vomits blood from oesophageal varices with known cirrhosis and shock. Banding fails with torrential flow. The team considers gastric coronary vein embolisation alongside pressure-lowering shunts. Which variceal logic best pairs vein closure with portal decompression?

items.q: A 54-year-old man has haemobilia with melaena and right upper quadrant pain ten days after liver biopsy. CT shows a hepatic pseudoaneurysm feeding the bile ducts. Which fistula logic best explains blood entering bile through biopsy-track pseudoaneurysms?
o: Arteriobiliary tracks shunt arterial blood into bile ducts
items.exp:
**Answer: A - Arteriobiliary tracks shunt arterial blood into bile ducts.** Biopsy needles bridge arteries to ducts where pseudoaneurysms pulse blood into bile with each heartbeat.
**Why the others are wrong**
- B: Needles bridge vessels to ducts
- C: Bile ducts bleed only when breached
- D: Melaena follows haemobilia classically
**Key point:** Biopsy haemobilia means arteriobiliary tracks.
r: Correct. Tracks shunt blood to bile.
items.kp: Post-biopsy haemobilia means arteriobiliary fistula.

items.q: A 61-year-old woman has the same hepatic pseudoaneurysm coiled with sac packing preserving the parent artery. Her melaena stops within a day. Which sac-preservation logic best explains parent-artery sparing in hepatic pseudoaneurysms?
o: Pack sacs while sparing livers that live off parent flow
Sacrifice whole livers for small sacs

**Answer: A - Pack sacs while sparing livers that live off parent flow.** Livers depend on arterial flow where portal flow fails, so sacs fill while parents stay open.
**Why the others are wrong**
- B: Whole livers never die for sacs
- C: Untreated sacs rupture onward
- D: Parents feed whole lobes
**Key point:** Hepatic sacs pack with parents spared.
items.kp: Hepatic pseudoaneurysms pack with parent preservation.

items.q: A 73-year-old man has a bleeding aortoenteric fistula with herald melaena after prior aortic grafting. CT shows graft-adjacent duodenal thickening with tiny bubbles. Which graft-emergency logic best treats herald bleeding in aortoenteric fistulae?

items.q: A 50-year-old woman has ongoing transfusion needs reviewed after gut embolisation with stable observations and no re-bleed. The team continues acid suppression with iron replacement. Which aftercare logic best completes gut embolisation recovery without re-bleed?

Stop all drugs the moment bleeding pauses
